answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity a cumulative, verifiable work history rather than a free credential. New agents start with zero trust and earn reputation only through tasks peers attest to observing, so trust compounds from real output. Forging a thousand fakes forces an attacker to rebuild a full attested history for each one, so cost scales linearly with the count. Verifiers also flag anomalies: accounts drawing from one narrow grove of compute, an unnatural delta in quality, or a cluster behaving like one shared lagoon of identical patterns.
